comment: The operator's view of a governed agent running on a managed cluster.
This ships as a template rather than as an exported workbook on purpose.
Exporting a workbook from the portal bakes the subscription id, the
resource group and the workspace resource ids into serializedData as
literals; this repository is public and refuses to carry any of them.
Everything identifying is a parameter, and the workbook's own name is
derived with guid() at deploy time rather than committed.
serializedData is built with string() over a readable object below, so
the panels can be reviewed as JSON instead of as one escaped line.
Two data paths, because 'enabled' and 'arriving' are different claims:
the metric panels read Managed Prometheus (the plane's own /metrics,
scraped from the pod through an explicit NetworkPolicy allowance), and
the log panels read Container Insights. If a metric panel is empty the
scrape is not landing; if a log panel is empty the add-on is not
collecting. They fail independently and they say so separately.

metadata.description: Run identifier; makes the workbook name unique per lift so two runs never collide.

content.json:
## The governance plane

Every panel below is the plane answering for itself. **Decisions** is the one to read first: a governed agent that is working shows allowed calls, and a governed agent that is being stopped shows denials with a reason. An empty Decisions panel means no agent has called anything yet — not that nothing is being enforced.

**Seam degraded** is the alarm. It is 1 while a seam refuses everything because its audit or ledger write last failed. That is the plane failing closed, which is the behaviour we want, but it means work is being rejected and somebody should know.

content.title: Decisions per second, by outcome and reason
What was refused in the last hour, and why
Time an admitted call spent at its upstream (p95, seconds)
Which build of the plane is answering

content.json:
## What the plane said

Container Insights collects stdout and stderr from every pod in the `kaimahi` namespace. The plane logs a line per governance decision, so this is the same story as the panels above told in prose — and it is where a failure that never became a metric shows up.

content.query:
ContainerLogV2
| where PodNamespace == 'kaimahi'
| project TimeGenerated, PodName, ContainerName, LogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 200
content.title: Recent plane log lines

content.query:
KubePodInventory
| where Namespace == 'kaimahi'
| summarize Restarts = max(PodRestartCount) by Name, ControllerName, bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
content.title: Pod restarts in the plane's namespace
